articles.headline: Meeting of the South Carolina Conference
articles.summary: We copy the following report of the proceedings of the above named Conference from the columns of the Charleston Courier. We are much pleased and gratified to know that the Courier has made such full and favorable notice of each day's proceedings. Our special thanks are due to Rev. James Lynch for sending us a copy of the report.

articles.headline: Correction. A False and Ignorant Issue taken against the African Methodist Episcopal Church, and a Correction thereof
articles.summary: There seems to have been a false issue taken, either through malice or ignorance, in regard to the shade of color or hue that constitutes and is to constitute the membership of the African Methodist Episcopal Church. We stand here, at the head of the Church paper, to advocate and assert her rights as an Evangelical Church.

articles.headline: A Tardy Jury
articles.summary: On last Thursday, 25th inst., five old colored residents of this city were returning from their day's work, (cleaning a load of carpets,) and when crossing the corner of 15th [VERIFY] and Washington Avenue met with a painful accident, by which two of the number lost their lives. It appears that a locomotive belonging to the Phila. W. and B. R. R. was running up and down the track with no cars attached.
people: survivor; 'well known in our midst'; jumped from the wagon
killed (printed 'Wm. Rhodes' here, 'William Rhodes' in the death notice on page 3)
killed (name as in the death notice on page 3)

articles.headline: At Bethel Church
articles.summary: Rev. William Offer, who intends sailing for California shortly, will preach in Bethel church on Sabbath next, at 3 P. M. Go and hear him.

articles.headline: Hurst St. Wesley Church
articles.summary: Divine service will be held in this church as usual, three times a day, the good Lord permitting. We shall preach a sermon on Sabbath next, with Divine permission. The subject chosen is, 'Who comforteth us in all our tribulation?'

articles.headline: The Colored Lincoln Monument
articles.summary: The colored people intend erecting an Educational Monument to the memory of Abraham Lincoln, to be located in Washington, and known as such. The officers who have been selected are as follows: President, Rev. H. H. Garnet. Vice Presid't, James Wormley. Rev. Stephen Smith, Treasurer. Walker Lewis, Assistant. Mr. Lewis A. Bell, Recording Secretary. William J. Wilson, Corresponding Secretary.

articles.headline: Personal
articles.summary: Rev. Dr. A. T. Wood, of the Indiana Conference, arrived in our city, last Sabbath morning. He came to our residence while we were engaged in family devotion. He preached a very fine discourse on Sabbath morning, in Bethel Church, and in the afternoon in Wesley Church.

articles.headline: The South Carolina Conference
articles.summary: It will be seen that this Conference has progressed finely, and exerted a wonderful influence in the city of Charleston. But we are sorry to see the Rev. Mr. Lewis, of the Methodist Episcopal Church, behave the way he does, if our correspondent be correct in his statement.

articles.headline: Twenty-Fourth Regiment
articles.summary: We have received several letters from some of our brave boys in the 24th Regiment, and our prayers are, that they may succeed well, and that their officers may treat them according to the rules of military regulations.

articles.headline: A First-Class Lodging and Boarding House
articles.summary: Mrs. Anne E. Foster, formerly of Baltimore, but now of this city, has just opened a first-class boarding house at No. 1733 Addison street, Philadelphia. Persons passing through our City of Brotherly Love, as well as our permanent residents, will find every accommodation at this establishment.
people: boarding-house keeper, No. 1733 Addison street (Mrs.; the ad on page 3 prints 'Mrs. Ann E. Foster')

articles.headline: Bishop Wayman's Address. To the members of the Philadelphia Annual Conference on the 23d day of May, 1865
articles.summary: Dear Brethren: It is usual for the presiding officer to deliver an address at the opening of the Conference, but I have deferred what I have to say until the close. Twenty years ago, I stood at the altar of this Conference, and took upon me the vows of an itinerant preacher. There are but two travelling preachers now present, who were members of the Philadelphia Conference then.

articles.headline: Death of Mr. Thomas Hamilton, of the Anglo-African (letter)
articles.author: J. P. C.
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: I have to announce to you the sad intelligence that Mr. Thomas Hamilton, late of the Anglo-African, and brother of Mr. Robert Hamilton, the respected editor of that paper, departed this life yesterday morning, Monday, May 29th, 1865, after a short illness of one week and one day's confinement to his room.

articles.headline: Sermon by Bishop Campbell. 'The War and Its Issues'
articles.summary: Report of a lecture by Bishop Campbell on the war and its issues at the Powell street African M. E. church (San Francisco), reprinted from a California paper; it runs over to page 3. There the Bishop says colored people are now allowed to testify in the courts and, in Washington and Alexandria, to ride in the street cars; he believed they had been allowed that privilege here (San Francisco) by Judge Pratt's decision.

articles.headline: Letter from Lieutenant-Colonel Trippe
articles.author: Lieutenant-Colonel Trippe
articles.summary: A letter from Camp Casey commending the young men enlisted in Philadelphia and trained at Camp William Penn. 'There is Sergeant Stephen F. R. Burdy [VERIFY], Sergeant Simpson, and William H. Rox [VERIFY]. All of these named gentlemen have proved themselves to be men and soldiers in every respect by their praiseworthy efforts to elevate their race.' They are engaged in teaching school and instructing the uneducated. Signed Lieutenant-Colonel Trippe, Commanding 24th Regt. U. S. C. T.; Chas. H. Potter, Acting-Adjutant.

articles.headline: Information Wanted (two notices)
articles.summary: Of Asberry or Rousbey Henry, who was sold from Hagerstown, Maryland, to Tallahassee, Florida, in 1838. When last heard from, in 1847, he was at the latter place. Any information of his whereabouts will be most thankfully received by his father, Rev. Thomas W. Henry, care Rev. E. Weaver, Box 2975, Philadelphia. Second notice: information wanted of Mrs. Sally Wallace, wife of Armstead Wallace, formerly of Brentsville, Prince William County, Va., and of Kitty Williams and the Beckly brothers, by Elizabeth Ann Jackson, Crawfordsville, Indiana.

articles.headline: Notice. First class accommodations for boarders and lodgers
articles.summary: First class accommodations for boarders and lodgers, by Mrs. Mary Stroder, 1132 Lombard St., Philadelphia. May 20, 3t.

articles.headline: Acknowledgments
articles.summary: Freehold, N. J., Mrs. J. A. Ludlow, $1 25; Denver, Colorado, W. J. Harden, 1.50; Davenport, Iowa, P. C. Cooper, for self and W. Vanderse, 1.25 each; City Point, Va., Corporal W. Gipson, for Mrs. R. J. Gipson, 2 00; Delaware Water Gap, Pa., C. V. Smith, 1 25. Also: West Philadelphia, Pa., Rev. Peter Gardner, for Hannah Butler, 1.25; Barrancas, West Florida, Rev. Enoch K. Miller, Chaplain 25th U. S. C. T., for one hundred and ten subscribers in the Regiment, 275.00.

articles.headline: Married
articles.summary: On the 27th day of April, 1865, by the Rev. William Murphy, William Matthews to Rachel Johnson, both residents of Chichester, Pennsylvania. May 4th, 1865, by Rev. J. C. Cornish, Mr. Henry Lyons to Miss Mary Wright, of Germantown, Pa.

articles.headline: Died
articles.summary: Killed, by being run over by a locomotive of the Philadelphia, Wilmington & Baltimore Railroad, on the 25th day of May, William Rhodes and Alex. Thompson, both old residents of Philadelphia.

articles.headline: To The Travelling Public. No. 1733 Addison Street, Philadelphia. Boarding and Lodging House
articles.summary: I most respectfully inform my friends and the public generally, that I have taken the large and commodious dwelling, No. 1733 Addison Street, Philadelphia, and have opened it as a first-class Boarding and Lodging House. I beg leave to refer to Mr. James W. Brown, Philadelphia. Mrs. Ann E. Foster. N. B. Hot and Cold Baths. Terms reasonable.
people: proprietor, boarding and lodging house, No. 1733 Addison Street (Mrs.)

articles.headline: A Card. Mrs. H. T. O'Donnell, boarding house
articles.summary: Mrs. H. T. O'Donnell, formerly of No. 740 South St., Philada., has removed to No. 913 [VERIFY number] Lombard Street, and has opened a boarding house for the accommodation of Ladies and Gentlemen who may pass through Philadelphia, and also those who may wish to spend some time in our city. May 1, 6mo.
people: boarding-house keeper, Lombard Street; formerly of No. 740 South St. (Mrs.)

articles.headline: Ice Cream Saloon. J. J. Lyons
articles.summary: Ice Cream Saloon. J. J. Lyons, No. 1023 Lombard Street, Philada., invites all lovers of Ice Cream and other delicacies to give him a call.
people: proprietor, ice cream saloon, No. 1023 Lombard Street

articles.headline: Private Boarding at 633 Pine Street, Philadelphia
articles.summary: The Subscriber, having fitted up his house with care, takes pleasure in announcing to his friends and acquaintances travelling that he is prepared to accommodate them when visiting the city. Warm and Cold Baths. R. H. Gleaves, Proprietor. April 29, 6mos.

articles.headline: Mrs. S. Shorter Hawkins: Spring & Summer Goods
articles.summary: Mrs. S. Shorter Hawkins would respectfully call the attention of her friends and the public generally to a well selected stock of Spring & Summer Goods, which will be sold at the lowest cash prices. Balmorals and hoop-skirts. Call and see at the old stand, S. Shorter Hawkins, 615 Lombard Street, Philada.

articles.headline: W. R. DeCordover's Periodical Depot
articles.summary: W. R. DeCordover's Periodical Depot, 419 South Seventh Street, Philada. New York Ledger, Anglo-African, Harper's Weekly, &c., for sale. Daily and Weekly papers always on hand. Also, stationery.
people: proprietor, periodical depot, 419 South Seventh Street

articles.headline: James O. Clark, M. D. (Eclectic.)
articles.summary: James O. Clark, M. D. (Eclectic.) No. 618 Pine Street, Philadelphia, Pennsylv'a. Office hours. Particular attention directed to all classes of Ulcers. Treatment and cure, without the use of Mercury, or any other injurious drug, warranted.
people: eclectic physician, No. 618 Pine Street (M. D.)

articles.headline: Trimmings and Fancy Goods. 633 Pine Street, Philada. Georgina Gleaves
articles.summary: Georgina Gleaves has just opened a large assortment of Ladies' Trimmings, Hosiery, Gloves, Flannels, Balmorals and Hoop skirts. Gentlemen's Furnishing Goods. Combs, brushes, soaps, choice perfumery and fancy articles. A general assortment of Stationery. Ladies' Dresses and Under clothing made to order.
people: proprietor, trimmings and fancy goods, 633 Pine Street

articles.headline: Help Wanted. Agency for the employment of help, No. 1113 Pine Street
articles.summary: Help Wanted at Mrs. M. C. Gibbons' Agency for the employment of help, at No. 1113 Pine Street, Philada. Also operating on the Sewing Machine, together with fashionable dressmaking. Sept 24, 6m.
people: keeper of an employment agency and dressmaker, No. 1113 Pine Street (Mrs.)

articles.headline: Military Instruction given to companies, associations, &c.
articles.summary: Military Instruction given to Companies, Associations, &c. Terms Moderate. Address James J. Spelman, 1031 South Street, Philadelphia.

articles.headline: Meeting of the South Carolina Conference
articles.summary: We copy the following report of the proceedings of the above named Conference from the columns of the Charleston Courier. We are much pleased and gratified to know that the Courier has made such full and favorable notice of each day's proceedings. Our special thanks are due to Rev. James Lynch for sending us a copy of the report.

articles.headline: Letter from Darby
articles.author: E. Y. T. [VERIFY]
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: On Thursday evening, the members of the Penn Temperance Association gave an Emancipation Jubilee in Town Hall, Darby. Long before the commencement of the exercises, the Hall was crowded to its utmost capacity. A goodly number of our white friends were present, and took great interest in the proceedings.

articles.headline: A Pleasant Surprise
articles.summary: On Friday evening May 26th, a portion of the class under Rev. J. Frisby of Bethel A. M. E. Church, showed their appreciation of his kindness and devotion, by presenting him a gold headed cane, valued at about $57 [VERIFY]. The presentation speeches were made by Mrs. E. Evans and Miss E. Lancaster, on behalf of the donors.
people: class leader, Bethel A. M. E. Church (Rev.)

articles.headline: Bishop Campbell's Arrangements [VERIFY headline]; The Bishop's Visit
articles.summary: The Indiana Annual Conference will meet on the third Saturday in August, in Springfield, Illinois. The Bishop wishes us to say, that he published in the Recorder that the Conference would meet at an earlier date. The Bishop's Visit: By divine permission, the Bishop will visit Cincinnati, last Sabbath in June; Louisville, Ky., first Sabbath in July; Richmond, Ind.; Indianapolis; Terre Haute; Chicago; Bloomington, Ills., second Sabbath in August.

articles.headline: Notice for the Indiana District
articles.author: Jabez P. Campbell
articles.summary: I will visit the following charges on my route to the Indiana Annual Conference, upon the following days, viz: Louisville, Kentucky, on the first Sabbath in July; Richmond, Indiana, on the 16th of July; Indianapolis, Indiana, on the 23d of July. Signed Jabez P. Campbell, Presiding Bishop. Philadelphia, Pa., May 31, 1865.

articles.headline: The Ohio and Baltimore Conferences
articles.summary: We are sorry to say that we have not had a single copy of the Minutes of the Ohio Annual Conference, notwithstanding our request to receive it. The Baltimore Conference, or the District Book Steward, has failed, up to the time of our writing, to send us a copy.

articles.headline: A Wide Mistake
articles.summary: We are continually receiving advertisements for insertion in our paper, but they are not accompanied by a single dollar. We cannot publish a paper for nothing, and we hope that persons who wish to advertise, will hereafter send the money with their advertisements.

articles.headline: Address to the Mayor of Philadelphia
articles.summary: By special request we publish the following address to his Honor, the Mayor of our city, which is an evidence of the loyalty of the colored people. To Alexander Henry, Mayor: We, the colored citizens of Philadelphia, and members of the Union Baptist Church, located in Minster St., between Lombard and Pine Sts., above Sixth street, assembled in our place of worship on Thursday last, the 1st of June, 1865, in compliance with the Proclamation of Andrew Johnson, President of the United States, for the observance of the obsequies of our late and lamented President.

articles.headline: Letter from Pittsburg: conduct of Philadelphia young men
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: We are sorry to expose any body to the public, but the conduct of some of your Philadelphia young men is too scandalous to be passed by unnoticed. William Dement [VERIFY], James Brooks, and Alexander Brown, of your city, came here, and boarded with us some time, and then slipped off without paying us for their board. Signed, proprietors (firm name unreadable), Pittsburg, Pa.

articles.headline: Notice: Quarterly Meetings of Attleborough Circuit
articles.summary: The Quarterly Meetings of Attleborough Circuit will be held as follows: June 17th and 18th, Buckingham Mountain; July 8th and 9th, Newhope; July 15th and 16th, Attleborough. T. Gould, Elder. J. P. Jay [VERIFY], Minister in charge.

articles.headline: Snow Hill Circuit
articles.summary: The Quarterly meetings of the Snow Hill circuit will be held as follows: Snow Hill, on Sunday, June 10th; Milford, Sunday, June 17th, and Jordantown, Sunday, June 24th. A. Till [VERIFY], Elder.

articles.headline: Notice: Quarterly Meeting of the Macedonia Station, South Camden
articles.summary: The Quarterly Meeting of the Macedonia Station, Spruce Street, South Camden, will take place on the 18th of June. G. E. Boyer [VERIFY], Minister in Charge.

articles.headline: Notice: Unity Lodge, G. U. O. of O. F.
articles.summary: We call the attention of our citizens to the advertisement of Unity Lodge, G. U. O. of O. F., in another column, announcing a grand anniversary demonstration, to come off at Sansom Street Hall, on Wednesday evening, the 14th inst. Tickets can be had of Mrs. James W. Brown, No. 1008 [VERIFY] Shippen street, who is one of the committee. Buy your tickets from Mrs. Brown; they are only 75 cents each.
people: member of the committee; tickets, Shippen street

articles.headline: Pennsylvania State Equal Rights Convention
articles.summary: The Minutes of the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights Convention, and Constitutions for State and subordinate Leagues, are now ready for sale, at the following rates: Minutes, $20.00 per hundred, 25 cents per copy; Constitutions, 5 cents per copy. Orders accompanied by the cash and postage, should be sent to Jacob C. White, Jr., Secretary of State League, 717 Lombard St., Philadelphia, Pa.
people: Secretary of State League, 717 Lombard St. (printed 'Jacob C. White, Jr.')

articles.headline: Acknowledgments
articles.summary: Cambridgeport, Mass., Maria A. Hatton, $1.50; Georgetown, D. C., Rev. J. Starbert; Louisville, Ky.; Port Deposit, Md., Rev. W. H. Hopkins, 6. (No Philadelphia names.)

articles.headline: Odd Fellows' Grand Demonstration. The Twenty-First Anniversary of Unity Lodge, No. 711
articles.summary: Odd Fellows' Grand Demonstration. The Twenty-First Anniversary of Unity Lodge, No. 711, of the Grand United Order of Odd Fellows, and of the introduction of the Order into the State of Pennsylvania, will be celebrated at the Sansom Street Hall, on Wednesday Evening, June 14, 1865. Tickets, 75 cents. To be had of the Committee.

articles.headline: Our National Fast
articles.summary: Never in the history of Philadelphia, has there been such a general or appropriate observance of a national fast day, as was noticed yesterday throughout our city. Business was entirely suspended. There was preaching in all the churches in the morning, and the invitation of the Committee of the Lincoln Monument Fund, asking that a collection be taken in the several churches, was read.

articles.headline: Greytown, Central America
articles.summary: Some twelve years since, a colored preacher of Philadelphia, felt moved to go to Greytown and preach the gospel to the people. He left all, and procured a lease of a lot, erected a church building and a dwelling, and has since been the recognized pastor of the people composing the Protestant congregation. His name is Benjamin Smith. After a few years residence in Greytown, he went to Canada and procured orders, under the authority of the Canadian Conference.
people: colored preacher of Philadelphia; pastor at Greytown, Central America

articles.headline: Meeting of the South Carolina Conference
articles.summary: We copy the following report of the proceedings of the above named Conference from the columns of the Charleston Courier. We are much pleased and gratified to know that the Courier has made such full and favorable notice of each day's proceedings. Our special thanks are due to Rev. articles.headline: Notice: Minutes of the Philadelphia Annual Conference
articles.summary: The Minutes of the Philadelphia Annual Conference are now ready at our office, No. 619 Pine St. Price 15 cents. Persons out of town can have them sent to them, by mail, for 20 cents per copy. June 16, tf.

articles.headline: Notice: Quarterly Meetings of Frankford Circuit
articles.summary: The Quarterly Meetings of Frankford Circuit, will be held as follows: Frankford, 1st Sabbath in July; Harrisburg Hill, 2d; Ben Salem, 3d; Bristol, 4th. J. H. Smith, Elder in Charge. June 16, 2t.

articles.headline: Notice: First Quarterly Meeting of the Zion Mission Church
articles.summary: The First Quarterly Meeting of the Zion Mission Church, 7th street, below Dickerson, Philadelphia, Pa., will be held on June 25th, 1865, Providence permitting. At which time we expect to have several worthy divines to assist. H. J. Rhodes [VERIFY initials], Pastor.

articles.headline: Married
articles.summary: On the 11th of June, 1865, by Rev. William Moore, Mr. William T. Sample of Kaighnsville, N. J., to Miss Fanny Robinson [VERIFY], of Philadelphia, Pa. In Bristol, Pa., on the 15th inst. [VERIFY day], by Rev. M. Taylor, Mr. Samuel W. Stockton [VERIFY], late of Philadelphia, to Miss Martha Lena Conn [VERIFY], of Burlington, N. J. In this city, on Sunday evening, May 28th, by the Rev. Theo. Doughty Miller, Mr. Paul Moore, of Virginia, to Miss Josephine Woodson, of this city.

articles.headline: Obituary: Johnson
articles.summary: JOHNSON. Died, in Chicago, Illinois, at the house of Polly Thrailkills, Thomas Johnson of Co. I, 25th U. S. C. T., on June 10th, 1865. The deceased was a resident of this city, and should this meet the eye of his relatives, they are requested to call at the office of the Christian Recorder, and obtain some very valuable information.
people: deceased; Co. I, 25th U. S. C. T.; resident of Philadelphia

articles.headline: Gov. Curtin to the People of Pennsylvania
articles.summary: Executive Chamber, Harrisburg, June 10, 1865. To the People of Pennsylvania: The bloody struggle of four years is ended. The survivors are now returning to us; I recommend that in every part of the State, on the approaching anniversary of Independence, special observances be had of welcome to our returned defenders. Signed Andrew G. Curtin, Governor of Pennsylvania. (General; no colored regiment is named.)

articles.summary: We copy the following report of the proceedings of the above named Conference from the columns of the Charleston Courier. James Lynch for sending us a copy of the report.

articles.summary: At the Annual Meeting of the District Grand Lodge, No. 2, of the I. O. of G. S. and D. of S. of the States of Pennsylvania and Delaware, held at the New Masonic Hall, South Eleventh street, Philadelphia, on Tuesday, June 6th, 1865, the following named brethren and sisters were duly elected and installed officers for the ensuing year. articles.headline: Festival
articles.summary: An entertainment was given by the Rev. S. T. Jones' Literary Society, at the Philadelphia Institute, on the 14th inst., for the benefit of the Missionary Fund of Wesley Church. Mr. Edward Evans, President of the Society, favored the audience with an address on 'The part the colored man has taken in the rebellion, and his rights as a citizen,' which was well received.

articles.headline: Unionville Correspondence
articles.summary: The true-hearted colored patriots of Unionville and vicinity, having somewhat recovered from the overwhelming stroke of sorrow so universally felt in consequence of the assassination of President Lincoln, determined to hold a meeting for the purpose of expressing their deep regret at our country's loss. The 27th of May arrived. The day was gloomy.

articles.headline: A Visit to the Public School in Brooklyn (in the editor's account of the New York and New England Conferences)
articles.summary: We paid a visit to the public school in Brooklyn, of which Mr. Dorsey, formerly of Philadelphia, is the talented Principal. There are three teachers in this school, including the Principal. The editor's account of the ending of the New York and New England Conferences fills the first three columns of the page.

articles.headline: Personal
articles.author: J. H. Turpin
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: On perusing your valuable paper a few days since, I saw an item relating to my appointment as a missionary to the Sunny South. Various circumstances compel me to defer my visit until another period. May the blessing of God go with Brothers Gibbs, Hedges and Thompson. Philadelphia, June 20, 1865.

articles.headline: Appointments for Indiana and Missouri Conferences; Episcopal Visits
articles.author: J. P. Campbell
articles.summary: The Indiana Conference will meet in Springfield, Illinois, on Saturday, August 19th, 1865. The Missouri Conference will meet in New Orleans, Louisiana, on Saturday, September 9, 1865. Episcopal visits: Cincinnati, Louisville, Nashville, Richmond, Indianapolis, Terre Haute, Chicago, Bloomington.

articles.headline: New York Conference Appointments; Appointments of the New England Conference
articles.summary: The following are the list of appointments made by the New York Annual Conference for the ensuing year: Bridge Street, James N. Williams; Fleet Street, J. Woodlyn; Sullivan Street, Henry Davis. The following brethren were transferred: Rev. R. H. Cain, South Carolina Conference; Revs. E. P. Gibbs [VERIFY initials], J. H. Hamilton, Wm. Watson and D. Seaton [VERIFY], Philadelphia Conference. From the New England Conference: Revs. W. W. Grimes, Jacob Mitchell, and W. S. Chase, to the Philadelphia Conference.
people: appointed to Fleet Street, New York Conference
appointed to Sullivan Street, New York Conference

articles.headline: An Acknowledgment
articles.author: Wm. Offer
articles.summary: The undersigned takes great pleasure in acknowledging the following contributions from his friends and well-wishers, to aid him on his journey to California: Bethel Church, Philadelphia, $26.00; Mt. Zion, New Brunswick, 25.00; Mount Zion, Trenton, N. J., 16.50; Bethel, Burlington, N. J., 7.00; Germantown, 6.00.

articles.headline: Notice: Quarterly Meetings of Burlington Circuit; Excursion
articles.summary: The Quarterly Meetings of Burlington Circuit will be held as follows: At Mount Holly on the first Sabbath in July; at Burlington on the third Sabbath in July; at Evesham on the fourth Sabbath in July. T. Gould, Minister. Excursion: The Pearl street A. M. E. Sabbath school, of Burlington, N. J., will make an excursion on Thursday next, June 29th. There will be a festival held in the basement of the church in the evening. T. Gould, Minister.

articles.headline: Information Wanted: Thomas T. Marshall
articles.summary: Information wanted of Mr. Thomas T. Marshall. When last heard from he was in Mound City, Illinois, preparing to go to St. Louis, Missouri. His grandmother, Rebecca Thorn, died lately in Charleston, S. C., and it is desired that he should go home immediately, and settle the estate, as he is the oldest heir. Any information will be thankfully received by Mrs. Charlotte Washington, 1117 Rodman Street, Philadelphia, Pa. June 24, 2t.

articles.headline: Obituary: Veazey
articles.author: Margaret Williams
articles.summary: VEAZEY. Killed, at Deerfield, 15 miles from Salem, New Jersey, on Wednesday morning, June 14th, John Veazey, by the falling of a roof which he was engaged in raising. He was a fine young man, highly esteemed and beloved by all who knew him. He leaves a wife, mother and sister to mourn his untimely end.
people: deceased; killed at Deerfield, N. J. (printed 'Veazey' and 'Vessey')

events.name: South Carolina Conference of the A.M.E. Church: first annual session at Charleston (second to fifth days)
events.location: Zion church, Calhoun street, Charleston, S.C.
events.description: Reprinted from the Charleston Courier, sent by Rev. James Lynch. The Conference met at Zion church, Calhoun street, Charleston, Bishop D. A. Payne presiding; religious services by Rev. R. H. Cain. Charles Bradwell of the Savannah Quarterly Conference was admitted into the itinerancy; local preachers were admitted and several men were elected to orders, among them Theophilus G. Steward and Jas. H. A. Johnson (the rest of these lists is too faint on the film to read with certainty). Rev. James Lynch offered resolutions on the educational work among the freedmen, thanking the American Missionary Association and the N. F. R. Association; he reported as chairman of the Committee on Missions. Rev. James A. Handy offered resolutions on the assassination of President Lincoln. Rev. R. H. Cain offered resolutions denying that the A.M.E. Church draws a distinction of color or excludes whites. Resolutions were passed to join in celebrating the first half century of the A.M.E. Church in April 1866. Stations and circuits were laid out: Savannah City Station (Union A.M.E. Church, formerly Andrew Chapel, and Wesley Chapel), Charleston City Station, Raleigh, Wilmington, Hilton Head, Beaufort River Circuit, Edisto and others. The printed list of appointments is too faint to read on this film. All persons named are missionaries and Southern preachers, not Philadelphians.

events.name: Two colored carpet cleaners killed by a locomotive at Washington Avenue; coroner's jury delays its verdict
events.description: On Thursday, May 25, 1865, five old colored residents of Philadelphia, returning in a wagon from a day's work cleaning a load of carpets, were struck at a crossing on Washington Avenue (cross street printed faintly, read as 15th [VERIFY]) by a locomotive of the Philadelphia, Wilmington and Baltimore Railroad running without cars. Horace Potter, 'who is well known in our midst', saw the locomotive and jumped. The two men seated at the rear of the wagon, Wm. Rhodes and Alexander Thompson, jumped or were thrown out and the locomotive passed over their bodies. The driver and Horace Potter and one Thos. (surname unreadable) were uninjured. The Recorder complains that the coroner's jury had not yet given a verdict, says no bell or signal was given, and rejects a daily paper's charge that the men were intoxicated: 'their sobriety can be vouched for by hundreds of our citizens'. The death notice on page 3 reads: 'Killed, by being run over by a locomotive of the Philadelphia, Wilmington & Baltimore Railroad, on the 25th day of May, William Rhodes and Alex. Thompson, both old residents of Philadelphia.'

events.name: Rev. William Offer preaches at Bethel Church before sailing for California
events.description: Notice: Rev. William Offer, who intends sailing for California shortly, will preach in Bethel church on Sabbath next (June 4, 1865) at 3 P. M.

events.name: Colored people's Educational Monument to Abraham Lincoln: officers selected
events.description: An Educational Monument to the memory of Abraham Lincoln is to be erected by the colored people at Washington. Officers as printed: President, Rev. H. H. Garnet; Vice President, James Wormley; Treasurer, Rev. Stephen Smith; Assistant, Walker Lewis; Recording Secretary, Mr. Lewis A. Bell; Corresponding Secretary, William J. Wilson. Only Rev. Stephen Smith is a Philadelphian; the others are of Washington and are given in the text only.

events.name: Bishop Campbell on the street cars (lecture 'The War and Its Issues', San Francisco)
events.location: Powell street African M. E. church, San Francisco
events.description: In his lecture at the Powell street African M. E. church, San Francisco, reprinted June 3, 1865, Bishop Campbell counted among the gains of the war that colored people were now allowed to testify in the courts and, in Washington and Alexandria, to ride in the street cars. He believed they had been allowed that privilege in San Francisco by Judge Pratt's decision. He told how he got on a car in Washington before colored people had been allowed by law to ride in the cars of that city, and heard the conductor and driver say that if the bill then in Congress ever passed there would be a rebellion in Washington: 'A rebellion to be inaugurated by drivers and conductors of street cars! The law passed, but who ever heard of the threatened rebellion?' He had travelled from Washington to Baltimore and from Baltimore to Philadelphia without a pass. No Philadelphia car item appears in this issue; this is the only street car passage in the four June issues.

events.name: Penn Temperance Association: Emancipation Jubilee at Darby
events.description: The members of the Penn Temperance Association gave an Emancipation Jubilee in Town Hall, Darby (Delaware County, Pa.) on a Thursday evening (date not given; the letter is printed June 10, 1865). The hall was crowded and a number of white friends attended. After singing and prayer a fac-simile of the Emancipation Proclamation and a portrait of the late President were presented to the Association, the first by Georgianna Thompson [VERIFY] and the second by E. Y. Dingle [VERIFY]. Isaac Carr [VERIFY] was the first speaker; the next was Samuel Thompson [VERIFY], a young man who had never before appeared in public; George Sanford [VERIFY] spoke on 'The Rebellion is Ended'. A colored soldier from the army and E. Y. Dingle [VERIFY] followed. A party of singers from Philadelphia furnished the music. A collection was taken up for the Presidential Monument. The print is very faint on the film and no name in this item could be read with certainty; none is linked.

events.name: Bethel A.M.E. Church: class of Rev. J. Frisby presents him a gold headed cane
events.location: Bethel A. M. E. Church, Philadelphia
events.description: On Friday evening, May 26, 1865, a portion of the class under Rev. J. Frisby of Bethel A. M. E. Church presented him with a gold headed cane, valued at about $57 [VERIFY]. The presentation speeches were made by Mrs. E. Evans and Miss E. Lancaster on behalf of the donors. The names of the donors as printed: Elizabeth Evans, Diana Bristo [VERIFY], Emma Lancaster, Rebecca Turner, Rachel Cassidy [VERIFY], Mrs. ---- Davis, Mary Brown, Annie Peters, Rachel Green, Miss ---- Chew, Hannah Turner, Henry Clark, Wm. Stokes, J. Fountain, W. Thompson, S. Evans, Mr. ---- Daniels, Frances Valentine, Charlotte Bostic [VERIFY], J. Thompson, Mary Gibson, Charlotte Stevens.
attendees: class leader, Bethel A. M. E. Church (Rev.); recipient

events.name: Union Baptist Church (Minster St.): day of mourning service for President Lincoln and collection for the Lincoln Monument Fund
events.location: Union Baptist Church, Minster St. between Lombard and Pine Sts., above Sixth street, Philadelphia
events.description: On Thursday, June 1, 1865, the day appointed by President Johnson's proclamation, the colored citizens of Philadelphia who are members of the Union Baptist Church, 'located in Minster St., between Lombard and Pine Sts., above Sixth street', met in their place of worship. Though few were present, after prayers they lifted a collection of $8.31 [VERIFY amount], which they sent to Mayor Alexander Henry to be deposited in the Lincoln Monument Fund, with an address. Signed by the Committee: Joseph Washington, John Boling [VERIFY], James Felix [VERIFY], Reuben Coots [VERIFY].

events.name: Unity Lodge, No. 711, Grand United Order of Odd Fellows: twenty-first anniversary and Grand Demonstration
events.description: The twenty-first anniversary of Unity Lodge, No. 711, of the Grand United Order of Odd Fellows, and of the introduction of the Order into the State of Pennsylvania, to be celebrated at the Sansom Street Hall on Wednesday evening, June 14, 1865. Addresses to be delivered by the Grand Master of the Order, Brother James McC. Crummill [VERIFY spelling], P. G. M.; Brother David B. Bowser, P. G. M.; Brother Charles F. Jones [VERIFY middle initial], P. G. M. Brother Charles B. Colly [VERIFY] will preside. A silver-plated ice pitcher will be presented to the member of the Ladies' Committee selling the largest number of tickets. Tickets 75 cents, to be had of the Committee; the editor's notice on page 2 names Mrs. James W. Brown, Shippen street, as one of the committee selling tickets.

events.name: Frankford Circuit (A.M.E.): quarterly meetings for July 1865
events.description: Quarterly meetings of the Frankford Circuit: Frankford, first Sabbath in July (July 2, 1865); Harrisburg Hill, second Sabbath; Ben Salem, third Sabbath; Bristol, fourth Sabbath. Signed J. H. Smith, Elder in Charge (confirmed on the June 24 printing).

events.name: Zion Mission Church, 7th street below Dickerson: first quarterly meeting
events.location: Zion Mission Church, 7th street below Dickerson, Philadelphia
events.description: The First Quarterly Meeting of the Zion Mission Church, 7th street, below Dickerson, Philadelphia, to be held on June 25, 1865, with several divines expected to assist. Signed H. J. Rhodes [VERIFY initials], Pastor.

events.name: District Grand Lodge, No. 2, Independent Order of Good Samaritans and Daughters of Samaria (printed 'I. O. of G. S. and D. of S.'), of Pennsylvania and Delaware: annual meeting, election and installation
events.location: New Masonic Hall, South Eleventh street, Philadelphia
events.description: Annual Meeting of the District Grand Lodge, No. 2, of the I. O. of G. S. and D. of S. of the States of Pennsylvania and Delaware, held at the New Masonic Hall, South Eleventh street, Philadelphia, on Tuesday, June 6, 1865. events.name: Rev. S. T. Jones' Literary Society: entertainment for the Missionary Fund of Wesley Church
events.description: An entertainment given by the Rev. S. T. Jones' Literary Society at the Philadelphia Institute (Lombard Street above Seventh) on June 14, 1865, for the benefit of the Missionary Fund of Wesley Church. Mr. Edward Evans, President of the Society, gave an address on 'The part the colored man has taken in the rebellion, and his rights as a citizen'. Music: Mr. Joseph Freeman presided at the melodeon, and popular songs were given by members of the society and others. The whole was under the management of Mr. C. E. Evans; the assemblage dispersed at 12 o'clock. Amount realized, $45.50.

events.name: Unionville (Chester County): colored citizens' two-day memorial meeting for President Lincoln
events.location: A. M. E. Church, Unionville, Chester County, Pa.
events.description: A meeting of the colored people of Unionville and vicinity on Saturday, May 27, 1865, moved from the grove to the A. M. E. Church because of rain; called to order by the President and Chief Marshal of the day, Speakman Miller. Rev. Jno. W. Stevenson, of Oxford Circuit, made the opening address; Geo. Morris, Esq., Rev. Wm. D. Johnson of Ashmun Institute and others delivered eulogies. The meeting continued on the Sabbath (May 28): Rev. Jno. W. Stevenson presided, Rev. Wm. D. Johnson prayed, and the author and traveller Bayard Taylor addressed the meeting and read a communication from the late President on the education of the freedmen; P. P. Hodges of Ashmun Institute spoke; the afternoon orator was John Stebbins, M. D. In the evening Rev. Wm. D. Johnson preached in the A. M. E. Church, followed by Rev. John W. Stevenson, the former pastor. Chester County names are given in the text only, except the Philadelphia Conference minister.

events.name: New York and New England Conferences: ministers transferred to the Philadelphia Conference
events.description: Printed with the appointment lists of the two conferences (June 1865). From the New York Conference: Rev. R. H. Cain transferred to the South Carolina Conference; Revs. E. P. Gibbs [VERIFY initials], J. H. Hamilton, Wm. Watson and D. Seaton [VERIFY] to the Philadelphia Conference. From the New England Conference: Rev. G. H. Rue to the Baltimore Conference, and Revs. W. W. Grimes, Jacob Mitchell and W. S. Chase to the Philadelphia Conference. Former Philadelphia ministers in the New York list: J. Woodlyn (Fleet Street), Henry Davis (Sullivan Street), John Frisby (Westchester circuit; first letters faint). Rev. H. J. Johnson presides over the New England missions.

events.name: Contributions of the Philadelphia district churches for Rev. Wm. Offer's journey to California
events.description: Wm. Offer acknowledges contributions to aid him on his journey to California: Bethel Church, Philadelphia, $26.00; Mt. Zion, New Brunswick, $25.00; Mount Zion, Trenton, N. J., $16.50; Bethel, Burlington, N. J., $7.00; Germantown, $6.00; Salem, N. J., $5.00; Pennington, N. J., $5.00; Macedonia, Camden, $5.00; Bordentown, $4.40; Princeton, $3.50; Bishop Campbell, $3.00; Bethel S. School, Philadelphia, $1.24. The whole amount received from the brethren and friends of the Philadelphia district is $105. See the June 3 notice of his farewell sermon at Bethel.

events.name: Pearl street A. M. E. Sabbath school, Burlington, N. J.: excursion and festival
events.location: Pearl street A. M. E. Church, Burlington, N. J.
events.description: The Pearl street A. M. E. Sabbath school, of Burlington, N. J., to make an excursion on Thursday, June 29, 1865, with a festival in the basement of the church in the evening. Signed T. Gould, Minister.

notes: June 3 (Vol. V, No. 22, whole No. 231). Page 1: poetry; correspondence from Smithfield, Xenia and St. Louis (out of town, not entered); serial 'The Curse of Caste; or, The Slave Bride'; the South Carolina Conference report; 'How Shall Colored Citizens Get the Right to Vote' (reprinted essay, runs to page 2). The faint print of the right-hand columns of page 1 could be read only in part.

June 3 page 2 also carries: Charleston correspondence signed R. H. C., a letter to President Johnson, Wilberforce University and Louisville letters, a letter of Malcolm Ayres on a death (out of town). Not entered.

June 3 page 3: out-of-town ads noted in text only: Baniker House, Cape Island, N.J. (Mrs. Teagle, to reopen June 20); Miss Jane Jobs, boarding at Fairhaven, N.J.; Dr. J. W. Creek, physician and apothecary, Baltimore; Dandridge Kelly, restaurant, Baltimore; Washington Hotel, William Taylor, Georgetown, D.C.; Winston & Thomas, New Orleans; Freedmen's Employment Bureau, Brooklyn; Globe Hotel, William P. Powell, New York (page 4).

June 3 repeats, not re-entered: Olive Branch (814 Lombard), Mrs. M. Bennett, Miss Mary Still agent notice, Bustill wig makers (403 South Sixth), Lebanon Cemetery notice (J. C. White, J. Asher), N. L. Durham, T. J. Bowers coal (631/634 Lombard), Mrs. Maria Highgates (1026 Barley), Longfellow, Jane Johnson and Ann Wear, Duterte, Charnock, Mrs. C. E. Harding (713 Lombard), James W. Brown, Charles W. Brister, Book Depository, Avery College. White-run ads (Hopkins hoop skirts, John H. Stokes, Henderson's Capitol Clothing House, Costar, Perry & Co., Jones, Reimer, Matlack, Rodgers, railroad) skipped.
June 3 page 4, columns 1 to 4 (poetry, family and children's reading) were checked from the OCR headings only, not read from crops.
The Recorder's 'Rev. Stephen Smith, Treasurer' of the Lincoln monument is the Philadelphia lumber merchant and minister.

SECOND PASS, June 3: page 1 (all 7 columns) and page 4 (all 7 columns) read from 400 dpi crops, page 3 columns 1 to 3 read in full. Page 4 columns 1 to 4 hold poetry, 'Hens and Chickens', family and children's reading and a sketch; nothing in scope. The South Carolina Conference ordination and appointment lists were tried at 600 dpi: the station names can be read (Savannah city Station, Charleston city Station, Raleigh, Hilton Head, Beaufort, Edisto) but the preachers' names cannot. The boarding-house notice is settled from the clear May 27 printing (page 3, column 4) and the editor's May 20 puff: Mrs. Mary Stroder, 1132 Lombard St.

Owner's rulings applied: 'R. H. Gleaves' of 633 Pine Street = Richard H. Gleaves (linked as printed); T. J. Bowers, coal, 634 Lombard = Thomas J. Bowers the singer, brother of Henrietta Duterte (repeat ad, not re-entered).

June 10 (Vol. V, No. 23). Page 1: poetry; army correspondence by Chaplain Turner; Louisville, South Carolina and Charleston correspondence; a chaplain's letter; the serial 'The Curse of Caste'. Only the Letter from Darby falls within the Philadelphia rule. Page 1 is very faint on the film.

June 10 page 2 also has: 'The Right of Franchise' (editorial), the New School General Assembly, the Christian Commission, a letter on Manchester, England, letters from Beaufort, Wilmington N.C. and from Brother Spriggs, 'Ill treatment of colored people in Charleston' (out of town). Not entered. The two Information Wanted notices repeat from June 3.

June 10 page 3: the obituary is of Father Adams of Vicksburg, Miss., by H. R. Revels (out of town). No marriages or deaths of Philadelphians were found in this issue. The ads on pages 3 and 4 repeat those of June 3 (Foster, O'Donnell, Lyons, Gleaves, Hawkins, DeCordover, Clark, Spelman and the standing ads); not re-entered.

The Equal Rights League secretary's address, 717 Lombard St., is the building of the Continental Restaurant and the Philadelphia Institute (see the Brister ad). James W. Brown the steam dyer advertises No. 1002 Shippen St.; the lodge notice gives Mrs. James W. Brown's number as 1008 (faint).

SECOND PASS, June 10: page 1 and page 4 (all 7 columns each) read from 400 dpi crops; page 3 columns 1 to 3 read in full. Page 1 holds no Philadelphia item besides the Letter from Darby. Page 4 columns 1 to 4: poetry, 'Conversation for the Little Folks', 'Matters and Things in Olympus' (a satire); columns 5 to 7 repeat the June 3 advertisements with no new card or society notice. Added from page 3: 'Our National Fast' and the Greytown item.

June 17 (No. 24): only pages 3 and 4 survive on the film. Page 3, column 1 opens with the end of a letter on the franchise signed Benj'n M. Bond of a Massachusetts regiment (out of town); the Equal Rights Convention minutes notice (Jacob C. White, Jr., 717 Lombard St.) and both Information Wanted notices repeat from June 3 and 10. Other marriages printed are of Baltimore, Washington and Trenton couples (text of the paper only, not entered). Columns 2 and 3 are reprinted miscellany.
June 17 ads on pages 3 and 4 repeat the June 3 set (the Cape Island house is now spelled 'Banneker House'); not re-entered. Page 4 columns 1 to 4 are family reading (checked by OCR headings only).
The marriage by Rev. Theo. Doughty Miller is by the pastor of a Philadelphia Baptist church; identification not made here.

SECOND PASS, June 17: page 4 (all 7 columns) and page 3 columns 2 and 3 read from 400 dpi crops. Page 4 columns 1 to 4: poetry ('Coming'), 'Summerings', 'Woman's True Beauty', 'Our Dogs', 'Rearing Children'; columns 5 to 7 repeat the standing ads (Bowers, Gleaves, Globe Hotel, Madame Tilmon's agency in New York, Matlack, Brooklyn bureau, the Book Depository catalogue, Mrs. M. C. Gibbons' Intelligence Office at 1113 Pine, Longfellow, Johnson and Wear, Duterte, Charnock, Harding, Avery College, James W. Brown, Brister, Spelman, Rodgers). No new card or society notice. The 'Intelligence Office' heading of the Gibbons ad is clear on this printing.

June 24 (No. 25). Page 1: poem by Rev. G. L. Mineley; an appeal of the Society of Inquiry of Missions of Wilberforce University; 'Letter from the Mountain City'; 'Our Church in Kentucky'; the serial 'The Curse of Caste' by Mrs. Julia C. Collins; a Tribune item on the Freedman's Savings Bank at Richmond; reprints on the churches and the colored race and General Butler on negro suffrage. Nothing within the Philadelphia rule was found on page 1; it was checked by OCR keyword search and sample crops, not read in full from crops.

June 24 page 2: the editor's account of the New England and New York Conferences, 'Education for the Freedmen', 'Universal Suffrage', army correspondence by a chaplain and a Wilberforce student's address were skimmed, not entered. Page 3: the Hannah Cole (New Bedford) and the two earlier Information Wanted notices, the Equal Rights minutes notice and the Conference minutes notice (price 15 cents, clear here) repeat. The married notice (Lafayette, Ind.) and the Brum obituary (Washington) are out of town. Page 4 and the page 3 ads repeat the June 3 set; not re-entered.

Obituary of John Veazey is signed Margaret Williams, No. 1115 Pine street, Philadelphia (author field). The signer of the Good Samaritans notice prints as 'William A. K. Smith' but in the roster as 'William A. R. Smith'.

'Brother Stephen Smith, R. W. G. Treasurer' of the Good Samaritans is recorded as printed; no identification with Rev. Stephen Smith is made here. 'Sister Maria L. Highgates' is probably Mrs. Maria Highgates of 1026 Barley street (shrouding ad); 'Sister Martha C. Gibbons' matches 'Mrs. M. C. Gibbons' of the 1113 Pine Street employment agency; Henry M. and Ann M. Cropper are the Olive Branch boarding-house family; Richard H. Gleaves is 'R. H. Gleaves' of 633 Pine Street.
The June 24 printing confirms the reading 'Asberry or Rousbey Henry' (Rev. Thomas W. Henry's son) in the Information Wanted notice first seen June 3.

SECOND PASS, June 24: page 1 and page 4 (all 7 columns each) viewed from 400 dpi crops reduced to montages (headings and most body text legible; a few faint passages in page 4 columns 1, 4 and 5 were not legible). Page 1: masthead, three poems, the Wilberforce missions appeal (T. H. Jackson, B. F. Lee, J. Shorter), letters from Frederick City (E. W. Hammond), Morrow, Ohio, Lexington and Danville, Ky., the serial, the Richmond savings bank item, 'The American Churches and the Colored Race' (quotes the Universe, the Irish Catholic paper of Philadelphia, against negro suffrage), General Butler on negro suffrage, a Canada letter on black refugees. No Philadelphia names. Page 4: poetry, 'The Fish I Didn't Catch', 'Making Fun of People', 'The Great Sanitary Fair at Olympus' (satire), 'The Oak', 'Gift Swindling', and the repeat ads. Nothing added.

Rechecks at 600 dpi: the Good Samaritans secretary is printed 'William A. R. Smith' in the roster (page 2) and 'William A. K. Smith' in the attestation (page 3); both readings are certain, so the inconsistency is the paper's. Mrs. O'Donnell's card reads 'No. 913 Lombard Street' on the June 17 and June 24 printings.

NOT FOUND after the second pass (pages read: June 3 pp. 1-4, June 10 pp. 1-4, June 17 pp. 3-4, June 24 pp. 1-4; page 2 of June 3, 10 and 24 was read by headings plus crops of the local columns, not every column in full): no Philadelphia street car item, no Institute for Colored Youth examination or commencement, no Equal Rights League meeting (only the notice of minutes for sale), no report of a returning colored regiment or of Camp William Penn beyond the Trippe letter (24th U.S.C.T.), and no Annual Conference appointments.
